Q: WSO2 MI – Error Could not write JSON stream when handling base64 payload A:

This is not a backend or mediation error. In WSO2 Micro Integrator, this happens when the response cannot be written back to the client.

your logs show the backend call succeeds(HTTP 201), and the faliure occurs later in:

JsonStreamFormatter.writeTo
PassThroughHttpSender.submitResponse

with,

Consumer error or stale connection has occurred

This means the HTTP connection is no longer available when MI tries to send the response. this can happen because client timeout, network interruption, large payload (e.g. base64) causing slow streaming or logging with json-eval($) forcing full message builiding.

So, you can try,

  • Remove or avoid logging full payloads (json-eval($))

  • Increase client/transport timeouts

  • Try with smaller payloads

optionally disable chunking

Q: CSS properties can't use measurement units other than pixels on Chrome A:

You can use units other than pixels, but you can't use em because they aren't computationally independent; there's no one single value that can be applied wherever the property is.

See e.g. MDN (emphasis mine):

If the value of the syntax descriptor is not the universal syntax definition, the initial-value descriptor has to be a computationally independent value. This means the value can be converted into a computed value without depending on other values, except for "global" definitions independent of CSS. For example, 10px is computationally independent—it doesn't change when converted to a computed value. 2in is also valid, because 1in is always equivalent to 96px. However, 3em is not valid, because the value of an em is dependent on the parent's font-size.

(The "universal syntax definition" is syntax: "*".)

Q: Using sed, is it possible to proceed addings, delition of lines and substitution in one shot A:

Judging from your posted codes, you may want to perform deletion within limited range (front matter). Then you can use sed 'start,end{/pattern/d}' filename syntax.

Would you please try something like:

sed -i.bak \
  -e '/---/,/---/{
      /heading: accordion/d
      /^meta:$/d
      /^  path:\?$/d
      s/  creation/__dc/
      s/  revision/__dc/
      s/  copyright/__cr/'} \
  -e '/__cr/a\__vs: 6' \
  *.md

Please note the quantifier ? must be escaped by \ when using BRE.

Q: Is php relevant today? A:

I think you are possibly reading some outdated materials or resources. First off, it is not a complete waste of time but please don't go too deep in it. You can learn jQuery on a high level if you truly want to know how things were done in the earlier days when vanilla JS couldn't do much and you want to know why React exist.
And for PHP, it is a backend programming language and some legacy codebases are still using it, however I don't think you need to invest heavily on it since you are a MERN stack developer unless there is an heavy demand for it. I will advise you continue learning NodeJs and becoming expert before thinking of other languages cos there are cool stuff you can do with Nodejs most especially in this era of AI.

Q: Connection Error:Oracle.DataAccess.Client.OracleException ORA-12170 A:

A similar SO question was solved when it was determined that the database was installed on a Windows box using DHCP. As I said in that answer, the Microsoft Loopback Adapter needs to be installed if you use DHCP on a Windows box with Oracle.
